newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FOCUS - Hungary's Postabank hit by panic withdrawals.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Hungary's Postabank hit by panic withdrawals.

text.p: Hungary's third largest bank, Postabank, was hit by a run on Friday as thousands of depositors rushed to withdraw their savings, but government and bank officials said there was no justification for the panic.
People queued for hours outside branches to withdraw their money after rumours circulated that Postabank had been hit by big losses.
"My husband just called me that Postabank went bust and I ran here to take out all our money," one woman, who declined to give her name, told Reuters.
There were reports of overloaded computers crashing in at least one branch office and windows smashed at another, but the crowds were mostly orderly, witnesses said.

Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said Postabank was solvent and bank officials said there was no truth to the rumours that the bank was in trouble. "The Postabank is solvent and liquid and it is only a rumour that was spread about the financial institution," Medgyessy told the Hungarian news agency MTI.

Postabank chairman Gabor Princz also denied the bank was in difficulty. "It is not true that Postabank has financial problems but it is partly true that there are rumours spreading in Budapest and it has a damaging effect on the bank," Princz told Hungarian Radio.

"I have to say that Postabank has been operating for nine years and I hope everyone is satisfied with our services," he said, adding that the bank had no plans to freeze accounts and would continue to pay out to depositors.

Bank officials said they could give no estimate of amounts that had been withdrawn, but queues of up to 500 depositors at a time jammed branches throughout Budapest. Postabank has a wide branch system, operating in part out of the nation's post offices.
In March last year it reported a pre-tax profit of 2.83 billion forints ($16 million) and had a balance sheet total of almost 270 billion forints at the end of 1995, up from 200.7 billion for 1994.

Major foreign shareholders listed in 1996 were Oesterreichische Postsparkasse, the Austrian postbank, with 10.4 percent, insurer EA-Generali with seven percent and Wiener Allianz with 0.2 percent. Other shareholders included Austria's GiroCredit and Volksbank.
Robert Muranyi, Postabank's deputy general director, said there was nothing behind the rumours.
"The bank is liquid," he told Reuters. "It increased its assets by more than 40 percent last year and is making a profit."

"We are able to satisfy all cash claims," he said, adding that even if people continued to take money out, the bank would be able to pay as it had "tens of billions" of forints which could be used for payouts.

"Another problem is that many newspapers use the PB abbreviation for Postabank and that is the same as the abbreviation of Polgari Bank, a smaller state-owned bank troubled with a huge 1996 losses," Muranyi said. ($ = 175.7 Hungarian Forints)
